When being attached to the debugger, I can invoke some diagnostic commands in Debug Console, like:

```javascript
// See all loaded modules and their paths
Object.keys(require.cache)

// Find specific module
Object.keys(require.cache).filter(k => k.includes('esbuild'))

// Get module details
require.cache['/full/path/to/module.js']

// For ES modules (if using Node 20.6+)
process.getBuiltinModule('module').Module._cache

// Current working directory
process.cwd()

// Environment variables
process.env

// Command line arguments
process.argv

// Node version and platform
process.version
process.platform

// Memory usage
process.memoryUsage()

// Loaded native modules
process.moduleLoadList
```

`"pauseForSourceMap": true` was a trick in launch.json configs to make the breakpoints work. Without this option I needed to add a `debugger` JS statement in the code.

I see that plugins (whether inline or referenced from `tsup.config.ts`) are loaded using `bundle-require` npm package and I can put a breakpoint there and see actual /home/ggrzybek/sources/github.com/grgrzybek/modular-app-showcase/packages/learning-js-tools/tsup.config.bundled_9x77jllwgcc.mjs file.

`bundle-require` actually calls real node's (dynamic JS) `import()` with the transformed temporary file!
